first.rationale: The two measured declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the highest-leverage single slot is the top of that funnel: onboarding completion is upstream of activation, and fixing it should propagate. memory_86 and memory_31 both point at simplification, which is why I want memory_86 pulled — it may be an independent onboarding-length result, or it may be a consolidated restatement of the same day-12 signup-field experiment, in which case I have one finding and not two, and my confidence should drop accordingly. memory_91 is the direct alternative (in-product activation messaging targets the larger -6% decline), so I want its source to see effect size and whether the lift was durable or a one-week nudge; if memory_86 turns out to be derivative and memory_91's effect is real and durable, I switch to activation_messaging. I am explicitly declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing being the most salient pressure: memory_73 records that it wins acquisition and revenue but materially damages 30-day retention and carries an explicit do-not-generalize caveat, which is disqualifying against a sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective — matching a price attack would buy accounts we then lose. referral_incentive (memory_57) is clean but operates on established customers and does nothing for the two metrics actually declining. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a different segment than the one under attack. Downstream value risk: memory_31's mechanism was cutting required signup fields, and those fields are plausibly what routes enterprise prospects into the sales-assisted path that memory_44 says produces better pipeline quality. So an SMB-activation win could quietly degrade enterprise pipeline quality — a metric this experiment would not measure. I therefore want the experiment instrumented to watch demo-request rate and lead-qualification completeness, not just activation, and to preserve any fields used for enterprise routing. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the underlying evidence is inherited and archived rather than freshly observed, the two supporting memories may collapse into one, and the enterprise-routing side effect needs a real measurement window before anything is generalized.

final.rationale: The verification changed my answer. memory_86 was lossy: the consolidated line read as an unqualified win, but the source (exp_86) records +13% completion and -2.1 days time-to-value alongside +9% 60-day churn concentrated in complex-workspace accounts, with an explicit do-not-roll-out instruction that the inherited summary dropped entirely. Acting on the summary would have shipped a change that trades measured completion gains for unmeasured churn in exactly the accounts worth the most long-term revenue. memory_91 verified clean in the other direction: +11% week-one engagement, +6% activation, and +1% 30-day retention — the retention number is the one that matters here, because it means the lift is not borrowed from the future the way promotional pricing's was. It also lands directly on the larger of the two declines; +6% activation is sized to the -6% quarter-over-quarter drop. So activation_messaging is the one direction with a verified source, a positive retention signal, and a match to the problem. Standard experiment rather than broad rollout: the effect is confirmed but was measured in a different period against a different competitive backdrop, and the day-76 declines may have a cause that messaging does not touch, in which case I want to see that in a measured window rather than after a full rollout. I am still declining promotional_pricing — memory_73's retention damage and explicit do-not-generalize caveat remain disqualifying against a sustainable-revenue objective, and note that memory_73 and memory_86 both carried caveats while memory_31 and memory_57 are now unverified summaries of the same consolidation process that already lost one caveat, so I hold those loosely. Downstream value risk: onboarding completion is still down 4% and I am not addressing it this week; simplify_onboarding remains viable but only if scoped to simple accounts with complex workspaces excluded, and if it is ever run it must preserve the signup fields that route enterprise prospects to the sales-assisted path memory_44 credits with better pipeline quality. I would also correct memory_86 in durable memory to carry its churn caveat, so the next agent does not inherit the same stripped version I did.
